evals.prompt: Web OAuth is disabled by our admin, so I need to authenticate the Atlassian CLI (acli) to our Jira Cloud site with a personal API token. Give me the exact login command.
assertions: Uses `acli jira auth login` (the per-product path), NOT `acli auth login` (which is the global OAuth path and does not accept an API token)
Feeds the token via STDIN — piped (`echo "$TOKEN" | acli jira auth login ... --token`) or redirected from a file — and NOT passed as a literal value after `--token`
Passes the site as the bare host `<site>.atlassian.net` (no `https://` prefix) with `--email`

evals.prompt: After I log in with acli, where does my Jira API token actually live? Is it sitting in plaintext in a config file I need to gitignore?
assertions: States that acli writes the token to the OS keychain natively (e.g. macOS Keychain, service `acli`) — you do not hand-store it
Clarifies the `~/.config/acli/*.yaml` files hold only non-secret profile data (site, email, account id, auth_type), not the token

evals.prompt: `brew install acli` fails with `Refusing to load formula atlassian/acli/acli from untrusted tap`. How do I install it?
assertions: Instructs to run `brew trust atlassian/acli` (or `brew trust --formula atlassian/acli/acli`) first, then re-run `brew install acli`
Does NOT suggest that acli is in homebrew-core or available as a cask — it ships from Atlassian's own tap

evals.prompt: Can I use acli to work with our self-hosted Atlassian Server / Data Center (including our on-prem Bitbucket)?
assertions: States acli is Atlassian Cloud only (`*.atlassian.net`) and cannot authenticate against a self-hosted Server / Data Center instance
Redirects self-hosted Bitbucket work to the REST-over-curl route (bitbucket-guide) rather than acli

evals.prompt: Find all Jira issues assigned to me that aren't done, from the terminal, as machine-readable output I can parse.
assertions: Uses `acli jira workitem search --jql "..."` with a JQL clause resolving the current user (e.g. `assignee = currentUser()` and `statusCategory != Done`)
Adds `--json` for machine-readable output rather than scraping the default table
